correctness.rationale: Convolution and radical-square-zero multiplication give [D+X,E+Y]_e=(d_u-d_v)y_e-(e_u-e_v)x_e. The signed incidence difference map on a forest is surjective with c-dimensional componentwise-constant kernel; choosing a tree potential basis yields c central elements and independent copies of [h_e,r_e]=r_e. The joint commutator is a direct sum of s-by-2 edge matrices. Their exact rank-0/1/2 counts prove the all-s polynomial and rank<=1 condition proves pairwise commuting counts. The radical annihilator dimensions independently certify that star and fence incidence algebras are not isomorphic or anti-isomorphic. Direct-basis exhaustive checks for q=2,3 and s up to 3, plus Lie basis checks for q=2,3,5, passed. Finite checks only corroborate the general proof.

Earlier one-element rank and two-element commuting-probability formulas are covered and explicitly not newly claimed. The exact cross-poset Lie normal form, full joint-centralizer distribution at every tuple arity, and genuinely higher commuting-tuple counts were not supplied by the inspected primary statements. The root-potential normal form is an original deduction in this comparison, with nontrivial residual risk that the short argument appears elsewhere.

value.rationale: The object is canonical: incidence algebras of height-one forest posets. The classification shows exactly what their commutator Lie structures forget, across every field, and provides a complete all-arity joint-centralizer invariant with exact closed multiplicities. Explicit star/path pairs for every m>=3 are associative-nonisomorphic even up to opposition yet Lie-isomorphic; this supplies infinite structural counterexamples to Lie-reduct rigidity, not a narrow numerical slice. Higher tuple distributions and higher commuting counts are natural nonredundant invariants motivated by the same structural question.
